course_description:
Introduction to occupational performance and exploration of human psychological and social functioning across the lifespan. Analyses their impact on the process of growth and development.

OCTY1203 continues to build on knowledge and skills introduced in first semester courses, supporting the development of professional identity and foundational occupational therapy practice skills.

This course introduces students to the range of personal and environmental factors that influence occupational performance and participation across the lifespan. Occupational therapy models, including the Person-Environment-Occupation (PEO) model, will be used to guide exploration of the developmental changes that occur within the person (biomechanical, sensory-motor, cognitive, intrapersonal, and interpersonal) from infancy to late adulthood, and the diverse environments in which occupational roles are enacted. Students will examine the dynamic interaction between person, environment, and occupation, and how these factors influence occupational performance across successive life stages.

Students will develop foundational clinical skills in observation, occupational analysis, communication, and assessment through tutorials, practical classes, and authentic learning experiences that replicate occupational therapy practice. Opportunities will be provided to apply clinical reasoning within simulated scenarios designed to reflect real-world clinical practice contexts. Communication, activity analysis, and professional behaviours introduced in first semester courses will be further developed and integrated throughout the course.

The course also supports the development of interpersonal and collaborative practice skills through group-based learning activities that prepare students for working effectively within healthcare teams and with clients. Authentic assessment tasks are designed to support the application of theoretical knowledge to occupational therapy practice and foster readiness for future clinical placements.

OCTY1203 runs in parallel with OCTY7810; however, tutorials, practical classes, and assessment activities are tailored to meet the unique learning needs of each student cohort.

Consistent with the profession’s commitment to person-centred and collaborative practice, OCTY1203 values the expertise and insights of individuals with lived experience. Lived experience perspectives are embedded throughout the course and contribute to student learning through involvement in assessment design, assessment processes, and dedicated learning activities, including a lived experience panel. These authentic contributions support students to develop a deeper understanding of occupational participation.

course_aims:
This course aims to develop understanding of the concept of occupational performance at different stages of development and thus provides a foundation for occupational therapy practice.ﾠ

Aspects of human biomechanical, sensory motor, cognitive, intrapersonal, and interpersonalﾠdevelopment will be examined alongside environmental factors (sensory, social physical and cultural context)ﾠwhich influence development. The dynamic interaction between personal and environmental factors will be discussed in relation to the acquisition of skills, occupational performance, and occupational roles across the lifespan.

Students will develop skills in assessing and analysing occupational performance and communicating the outcomes of this assessment to key stakeholders. Learning activities in the course provide opportunities to develop professional behaviour and skills required for ongoing professional development, including working collaboratively with peers, making evaluative judgements, and self-regulating learning.ﾠﾠ

learning_outcomes.description: Apply occupational therapy models to identify the elements of the person, environment and occupation which change across the lifespan, and explain how these changes are linked with occupational performance in occupational roles.
Explain how life circumstances (including health conditions and environmental factors - historical and current) impact occupational performance and roles.
Assess aspects of occupational performance following the protocol and scoring instructions of a standardised developmental assessment tool, and interpret findings of this assessment.
Work collaboratively with peers to analyse and assess occupational performance.

Convey the outcomes of the assessment of occupational performance to relevant stakeholders both verbally and in a written format, using professional language and expression appropriate to the audience.

Apply, demonstrate and evaluate strategies related to communicating openly, effectively and respectfully with peers and professional colleagues; as well as demonstrate skills and strategies related to working collaboratively with colleagues; and with relevant stakeholders.

assessment_details.title: Occupational Performance Summary Report AND Prac (fieldwork simulation)
assessment_details.task_description: Students are required to participate in both practical classes in Weeks 2 and 3. During these sessions, students will engage in an authentic clinical learning experience involving a paediatric case study and the scoring of a standardised occupational therapy assessment. Through participation in these practical classes, students will develop skills in: Assessing occupational performance in early childhood Administering a standardised assessment Scoring and interpreting assessment findings Communicating assessment outcomes using occupational therapy terminology The practical classes provide the assessment data, clinical information, and learning experiences required to complete Assessment Task 1, a written Occupational Performance Summary Report. Knowledge developed from participating in the practical sessions will also contribute to Assessment Task 2, the accompanying Oral Viva. These practical classes simulate authentic occupational therapy practice and provide opportunities to develop assessment, communication, and clinical reasoning skills. Students are expected to actively engage in both sessions, as the assessment-related information and learning activities provided during class will not be replicated elsewhere. The practical classes also contribute to students' practice-based learning experiences in preparation for the 1,000 hours of practice education required for graduation and professional registration. Due to client privacy and confidentiality requirements, materials such as video footage and clinical information will not be made available outside of class. Written Report (Paired) Working in pairs, students will prepare a professional occupational therapy report based on the paediatric case study and assessment information provided during the practical classes. The report will require students to communicate assessment findings and demonstrate their understanding of the child's occupational performance through the interpretation and analysis of assessment results and clinical information. The Written Report will be worth 35% of your overall mark and will be submitted as a pair via Learn.uq by 2pm Thursday Week 6. If a student does not receive a pass mark for their first submission, they will be eligible to resubmit the task. However, any approved resubmission will result in a maximum achievable mark of a pass (55%). Under no circumstances should identifiable clinical information be uploaded to open or external AI platforms, as it is unethical and irresponsible. Given this assessment is related to a real client please see more information on use of AI in student placements under additional assessment information. Students must clearly reference any use of AI in each instance using the AI declaration form. A failure to reference generative AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Lectures Weekly pre-recorded lectures (approximately 2 hours per week) provide foundational knowledge across a range of early-stage support and management topics. Lectures are not timetabled and will be made available via blackboard ultra each Monday for flexible viewing. Students are expected to engage with the lecture content prior to attending their scheduled tutorial, where concepts will be applied through discussion, case-based learning, and practical activities. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Wednesday Tutorials Tutorials will be held in person on campus during Weeks 1-13 of the semester. Each session will run for 2 hours and will incorporate inquiry-based learning and small group discussions to explore key concepts in greater depth. These sessions are designed as experiential learning activities, and participants are expected to attend and actively engage. To prepare, participants must complete view the lecture and complete any designated preparation tasks before each tutorial. As these sessions involve small group work, they will not be recorded. In Week 12, tutorials will be replaced by a combined lived experience panel. This session will provide students with the opportunity to hear firsthand perspectives and further explore the application of theoretical concepts to introduced in the course. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 3 (03 Aug - 16 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Prac Sessions (Weeks 2&3 only) Attendance at both practical sessions is expected, as these classes contribute to the 1,000 hours of practice-based learning required for graduation and professional registration. In weeks 2 and 3 students will attend two 2 hours in person practical sessions on campus. Students be introduced to a case study of a young child, which will form the basis for the developmental summary report and oral viva. As this is a small-group, interactive experience, it will not be recorded. Please note: These sessions provide essential hands-on experience and are foundational to the successful completion of the associated assessment tasks. Recording of video materials is strictly prohibited. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L05, L06
